words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.ex: His neck was stiff after sleeping wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他睡姿不对，脖子变得僵硬。
words.en: If something is stiff, it is firm and does not bend easily. It can also describe a person who is not relaxed or friendly.

words.ex: The rules remained unchanged.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则没有改变。
words.en: If something is unchanged, it has stayed the same for a particular period of time.

words.tr: phrase. 微小的改变；极少的变化
words.ex: There was little change in the weather today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气几乎没有改变。
words.en: A description of a situation where there is a minimal or insignificant alteration in a value or condition.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；重要的；影响明显的；
words.ex: This discovery is a significant step forward.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现是一个重大的进步。
words.en: Something that is significant is important or large enough to be noticed or to have an effect.

words.tr: adj. 急剧的；引人注目的；戏剧（性）的；
words.ex: There was a dramatic increase in temperature yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度急剧上升。
words.en: If something is dramatic, it happens or changes suddenly and noticeably.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；重大的；实质性的；
words.ex: He made a substantial profit from the sale.
words.ex_cn: 他从这次销售中获得了大量的利润。
words.en: Something that is substantial is large in size, amount, or importance.

words.tr: adj. 不同寻常的；非凡的；显著的；值得注意的；
words.ex: She made a remarkable improvement in just one month.
words.ex_cn: 她在短短一个月内取得了不同寻常的进步。
words.en: Unusual or striking in a way that attracts attention.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.ex: The trip takes approximately 30 minutes.
words.ex_cn: 这段旅程大约需要30分钟。
words.en: Used to indicate that something is close to the actual, but not completely accurate or exact.

words.ex: I nearly missed the bus this morning.
words.ex_cn: 我今天早上差点没赶上公交车。
words.en: Almost, but not quite; very close to.

words.ex: He almost finished his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他几乎完成了作业。
words.en: You use almost to indicate that something is not completely the case but is nearly the case.

words.ex: The proportion of students who passed the test was high.
words.ex_cn: 通过考试的学生比例很高。
words.en: A proportion is a part of a whole, or the relationship of one part to another in terms of size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: The percentage of students who passed the test was 85.
words.ex_cn: 通过考试的学生百分比是85。
words.en: A percentage is a proportion or ratio expressed as a fraction of 100.

words.tr: v. 给予；“give”的过去分词； prep. 考虑到； adj. 规定的；
words.ex: She was given a gift by her friend.
words.ex_cn: 她的朋友给了她一份礼物。
words.en: If you say 'given' something, you mean taking that thing into account.

words.tr: v. 考虑；“consider”的现在分词； prep. 考虑到；就…而言；鉴于；
words.ex: I am considering going to the park.
words.ex_cn: 我正在考虑去公园。
words.en: Taking into account; in view of.

words.ex: He spoke in regard to the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 他谈到了新的校规。
words.en: Concerning or about something.

words.ex: He believed his destiny was to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自己的命运是成为一名医生。
words.en: Destiny is the force which some people believe controls the things that happen to you in your life.

words.ex: There is a chance it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天可能会下雨。
words.en: A chance is a possibility of something happening, often something that you want to happen.

words.ex: He showed great capability in solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决数学问题上展现了很强的能力。
words.en: The ability or qualities necessary to do something.

words.ex: His competence in math helped him solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面的能力帮助他解决了这个问题。
words.en: Competence is the ability to do something well or efficiently.

words.ex: He has the ability to solve math problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力快速解决数学问题。
words.en: The capacity to do something or the possession of the means or skill to do something.

words.ex: The drought depletes the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 干旱耗尽了水源。
words.en: If you deplete something, you reduce the amount of it that is available or that exists.

words.tr:
v. 耗尽；用完；使筋疲力尽
n. 排气管；废气
words.ex: The long hike exhausted him.
words.ex_cn: 这次漫长的徒步旅行让他筋疲力尽。
words.en: If something exhausts you, it makes you so tired, either physically or mentally, that you have no energy left.

words.ex: He used up all the water.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的水都用完了。
words.en: To consume or exhaust something completely.

words.ex: He exploited the situation to get more money.
words.ex_cn: 他利用这个情况赚了更多钱。
words.en: To exploit someone or something means to use them in a way that benefits you, often unfairly or without considering their rights or feelings. It can also refer to the act of making full use of and deriving benefit from a resource.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.tr:
adj. 复杂的；
n. 综合楼（群）；
words.ex: The instructions are too complex for children.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明对孩子来说太复杂了。
words.en: Something that is complex has many different parts, and is therefore often difficult to understand.

words.ex: The math problem is complicated.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学问题很复杂。
words.en: Involving many different and confusing aspects.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.tr: n. 安全；保障；防护措施；
words.ex: The school improved security to protect students.
words.ex_cn: 学校加强了安全措施以保护学生。
words.en: Security refers to the state of being free from danger or threat, or measures taken to ensure safety.

words.ex: Please ensure the door is locked.
words.ex_cn: 请确保门锁好了。
words.en: To make certain that something will occur or be the case.

words.ex: He insured his car against accidents.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的车投保了意外险。
words.en: If you insure yourself or your property, you pay money to an insurance company so that if you become ill or if your property is damaged or stolen, the company will pay you a sum of money.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
words.ex: The store guarantees a refund if you are not happy.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不满意，商店保证退款。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if it is not of a specified quality.

words.ex: He solely depends on his bike to go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他只靠自行车去上班。
words.en: If something is solely the case, it is the only thing that is the case.

words.ex: He is merely a student.
words.ex_cn: 他仅仅是个学生。
words.en: You use merely to emphasize that something is only what you say and not better, more important, or more exciting.

words.tr:
adv. 只；仅仅；只有；
adj. 唯一的；仅有的；
words.ex: He eats only apples for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐只吃苹果。
words.en: You use only to indicate the one thing that is true, appropriate, or important in a particular situation, in contrast to all the other things that are not true, appropriate, or important.

words.ex: I assume it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假定明天会下雨。
words.en: If you assume that something is true, you accept that it is true without proof.

words.ex: I suppose he is late because of the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我认为他因为交通堵塞而迟到了。
words.en: If you suppose that something is true, you believe or imagine that it is true, although you may not have any proof.

words.tr:
v. 假定；要求
n. 假定；假设
words.ex: He postulates that all humans are equal.
words.ex_cn: 他假定所有人都是平等的。
words.en: If you postulate something, you suggest it as the basis for a theory, argument, or calculation.

words.ex: Scientists hypothesize that water once existed on Mars.
words.ex_cn: 科学家假设火星上曾经存在水。
words.en: To hypothesize means to suggest a possible explanation for something, which has not yet been proved to be true.

words.ex: His guess about the winner was just speculation.
words.ex_cn: 他对获胜者的猜测只是推测。
words.en: The act of forming opinions about what has happened or what might happen without knowing all the facts.

words.ex: The manager will authorize the payment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天将批准这笔付款。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen, or to give someone official permission to do something.

words.tr:
n. 委员会；佣金；
v. 委托；
words.ex: The commission met to discuss the new law.
words.ex_cn: 委员会开会讨论新法律。
words.en: A commission is a group of people who have been appointed to find out about something or to control something, or the act of doing this. It can also refer to a sum of money that is paid to someone for selling something, which is usually a percentage of the value of the goods sold.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.ex: Every worker has an entitlement to fair pay.
words.ex_cn: 每位工人都有获得公平报酬的权利。
words.en: An entitlement is a right to have or do something, often granted by law or policy.

words.tr:
adv. 正确地；直接地；向右；
adj. 正确的；右边的；
n. 右边；权利；
v. 纠正；
words.ex: He answered the question right.
words.ex_cn: 他正确地回答了问题。
words.en: If something is right, it is correct and agrees with the facts.

words.ex: The festival celebrates ethnic music and dance.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日庆祝民族音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Ethnic relates to a group of people who have a common national or cultural tradition.

words.ex: He faced racial discrimination at work.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中遭遇了种族歧视。
words.en: Relating to the common characteristics of different races of people, especially in the context of social or cultural differences.

words.tr: n. 道德规范；伦理标准；
words.ex: The company follows a strong ethic of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司遵循诚实的道德规范。
words.en: An ethic is a moral principle or set of moral principles that guides the behavior of a person or group, especially in a professional context.

words.tr:
adj. 道德的；道义上的；
n. 寓意；
words.ex: It is a moral duty to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 说实话是一种道德责任。
words.en: Concerned with the principles of right and wrong behavior and the goodness or badness of human character.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
n. 变化；变革；
v. 变化；变革；
words.ex: There was a big change in the weather.
words.ex_cn: 天气发生了很大的变化。
words.en: To make or become different; to alter or modify; to exchange or replace something with another.

words.tr:
n. 转移；移位；转变；轮班；
v. 变换位置；转移；换（挡）；轮班；
words.ex: The shift of power to the new government was sudden.
words.ex_cn: 权力向新政府的转移是突然的。
words.en: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves or changes its position slightly. If someone's opinion, attitude, or behaviour shifts, it changes slightly, especially in response to a particular situation or event.

words.ex: He revised his answer to make it correct.
words.ex_cn: 他修正了他的答案，使其正确。
words.en: To revise something means to alter or amend it, especially in order to correct or improve it.

words.ex: The new teacher transformed the class into a lively group.
words.ex_cn: 这位新老师把班级变成了一个充满活力的团体。
words.en: To transform something or someone means to change them completely and usually improve their appearance, form, or structure.

words.ex: He will alter the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会改动计划。
words.en: To alter something means to change it, usually slightly, or to cause the characteristics of something to change.

words.ex: His insight helped the team solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他的洞察力帮助团队解决了问题。
words.en: If you gain insight or an insight into a complex situation or problem, you gain an accurate and deep understanding of it.

words.tr: n. 知识；了解；学问；学识；
words.ex: He gained knowledge from reading books.
words.ex_cn: 他通过读书获得了知识。
words.en: Knowledge is information and understanding about a subject which a person has, or which all people have.

words.tr: n. 学习；学问； v. 学习；“learn”的现在分词；
words.ex: Learning takes time and practice.
words.ex_cn: 学习需要时间和练习。
words.en: The acquisition of knowledge or skills through study, experience, or being taught.

words.tr: n. 理解；了解； v. “understand”的现在分词；
words.ex: His understanding of the problem helped solve it quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题的理解帮助快速解决了它。
words.en: An understanding is a mutual agreement or sympathy between people or groups.

words.ex: Under these circumstances, we had to cancel the trip.
words.ex_cn: 在这种情况下，我们不得不取消旅行。
words.en: A circumstance is a fact or event that makes a situation the way it is.

words.ex: The children are playing in their natural surroundings.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们正在他们的自然环境中玩耍。
words.en: The things and conditions around a person, place, or thing.

words.ex: He protects the environment by recycling.
words.ex_cn: 他通过回收利用来保护环境。
words.en: The environment is the natural world in which people, animals, and plants live.

words.ex: He changed his job because of his background.
words.ex_cn: 他因为自己的背景换了工作。
words.en: The background is the situation that exists at a particular time, or the situation in which something happens, which helps to explain it.

words.tr: n. 环境；装置；镶嵌( setting的名词复数 )；
words.ex: The settings of the forest made it perfect for camping.
words.ex_cn: 森林的环境非常适合露营。
words.en: The physical environment, context, or background in which something exists or takes place.

words.ex: The word means different things in different context.
words.ex_cn: 这个词在不同的上下文中意思不同。
words.en: The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.

words.ex: Birds begin migration in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在秋天开始迁徙。
words.en: The movement of people, animals, or birds from one place to another, especially regularly according to the seasons.

words.tr: n. 运动；动作；活动；乐章；
words.ex: The movement of the sun changes the shadow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的运动改变了影子。
words.en: The act or process of moving or being moved; a change of position or place.

words.tr: phrase. 未固定的；未确定的；可变的；不稳定的
words.ex: The meeting time is not fixed yet.
words.ex_cn: 会议时间还未确定。
words.en: Not fixed means something that is not firmly set or determined and may be subject to change.

words.ex: The city became prosperous after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市变得繁荣了。
words.en: A prosperous person, place, or economy is rich and successful.

words.tr: adj. 繁荣的；旺盛的；兴旺的； v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；“thrive”的现在分词；
words.ex: The town is thriving because of its new factories.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇因为新的工厂而繁荣。
words.en: Prospering or flourishing; successful.

words.tr: v. 快速发展；“boom”的现在分词； adj. 急速发展的；暴涨的；繁荣发展的；
words.ex: The tech industry is booming.
words.ex_cn: 科技行业正在快速发展。
words.en: Experiencing a period of great prosperity or rapid economic growth.

words.tr: adj. 繁荣的；欣欣向荣的；繁茂的； v. “flourish”的现在分词；
words.ex: The town is flourishing after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 这家新工厂开业后，这个小镇变得繁荣了。
words.en: If something is flourishing, it is growing or developing in a healthy or vigorous way, especially as a result of a particularly congenial environment.

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.ex: The sky looks heavenly at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时天空看起来像天上的。
words.en: If you describe something as heavenly, you mean that it is extremely pleasant or enjoyable.

words.ex: The church is a holy place.
words.ex_cn: 教堂是一个神圣的地方。
words.en: If you describe something as holy, you mean that it is considered to be special because it is connected with God or a particular religion.

words.ex: The temple is a sacred place for believers.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙对信徒来说是神圣的地方。
words.en: Something that is sacred is considered to be holy or connected with God or a god.

words.ex: The frog is poisonous.
words.ex_cn: 这只青蛙是有毒的。
words.en: Something that is poisonous will kill you or make you ill if you eat it, drink it, or absorb it.

words.ex: The water is toxic to fish.
words.ex_cn: 这种水对鱼是有毒的。
words.en: If a substance is toxic, it is poisonous.

words.ex: The snake has a deadly bite.
words.ex_cn: 这种蛇的咬伤是致命的。
words.en: If something is deadly, it is likely or able to cause someone's death, or has already caused someone's death.

words.ex: The accident was fatal.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是致命的。
words.en: If an action or event is fatal, it causes someone's death.

words.ex: The poison is lethal to humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒药对人类是致命的。
words.en: Something that is lethal can kill people or animals.

words.tr:
n. 凡人
adj. 致命的；终有一死的
words.ex: All mortal beings must die someday.
words.ex_cn: 所有凡人都终有一死。
words.en: If you refer to the fact that people are mortal, you mean that they have to die and cannot live forever.

words.ex: He looks like his father.
words.ex_cn: 他看起来像他的父亲。
words.en: To resemble or seem similar to someone or something in appearance.

words.ex: The boy resembles his father.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩长得像他父亲。
words.en: If one thing or person resembles another, they are similar to each other.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.ex: He saves money for long-term goals.
words.ex_cn: 他为长期目标存钱。
words.en: Something that is long-term has continued for a long time or will continue for a long time in the future.

words.ex: The prolonged rain caused flooding.
words.ex_cn: 持久的降雨引发了洪水。
words.en: Something that is prolonged continues for a long time, or longer than expected.

words.tr: adj. 持久的；不朽的； v. 忍受；“endure”的现在分词；
words.ex: This is an enduring friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这是一段持久的友谊。
words.en: Lasting for a long time; continuing or enduring over a period of time.

words.ex: The therapist helped him feel better after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 治疗专家在事故后帮助他感觉好些了。
words.en: A therapist is a person who is skilled in a particular type of therapy and treats people using it.

words.ex: The physician checked the patient's temperature.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了病人的体温。
words.en: A physician is a medical doctor who is trained in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases and injuries.

words.ex: The surgeon fixed the broken bone.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生修复了断裂的骨头。
words.en: A surgeon is a medical doctor who performs operations.

words.ex: He visits the dentist every six months.
words.ex_cn: 他每六个月去看一次牙医。
words.en: A dentist is a person who is qualified to treat diseases and conditions that affect the teeth and gums, especially the repair and extraction of teeth and the insertion of artificial ones.

words.tr: n. 精神病学家；精神科医生
words.ex: He visits a psychiatrist every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周去看一次精神科医生。
words.en: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who specializes in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental illnesses and emotional disorders.

words.tr:
n. 专家；行家；
adj. 内行的；老练的；专门的；
words.ex: He is an expert in computer science.
words.ex_cn: 他是计算机科学方面的专家。
words.en: A person who is very knowledgeable about or skillful in a particular area.

words.ex: He is a specialist in heart surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他是心脏手术方面的专家。
words.en: A specialist is a person who is highly skilled or knowledgeable in a particular field.

words.tr: adj. 最常见的；最普通的
words.ex: This is the commonest mistake students make.
words.ex_cn: 这是学生最常见的错误。
words.en: Superlative of 'common'; most frequent or widespread.

words.ex: He makes frequent trips to the city.
words.ex_cn: 他经常去城市。
words.en: If something is frequent, it happens often.

words.tr:
adj. 退步的；堕落的；腐化的
v. 退化；堕落
n. 堕落的人
words.ex: The old machine became degenerate and stopped working.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器退步了，停止工作了。
words.en: If you say that someone or something degenerates, you mean that they become worse in some way, for example, poorer, weaker, or less respectable.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: The country has an underdeveloped economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经济不发达。
words.en: An underdeveloped country or region is one that is less developed economically and socially than most others, with many of its people living in poverty.

words.ex: This book belongs to the science category.
words.ex_cn: 这本书属于科学类别。
words.en: A category is a class or group of things that have similar characteristics.

words.ex: The teacher gave a classification of animals into mammals and birds.
words.ex_cn: 老师将动物分为哺乳动物和鸟类。
words.en: The action or process of classifying something according to shared qualities or characteristics.

words.ex: The accident had serious subsequence on his life.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故对他的生活造成了严重后果。
words.en: A subsequence is a sequence that can be derived from another sequence by deleting some or no elements without changing the order of the remaining elements.

words.tr: adj. 接着的；下列的； prep. 在...之后； v. 跟随；“follow”的现在分词； n. 下列各项；
words.ex: The following day, we went to the park.
words.ex_cn: 接着的那天，我们去了公园。
words.en: Coming after or as a result of something; a group of supporters or admirers.

words.ex: We ate dinner, and afterward we watched a movie.
words.ex_cn: 我们吃了晚饭，之后看了部电影。
words.en: If you do something or if something happens afterward, you do it or it happens after a particular event or time that has already been mentioned.

words.ex: The sequence of numbers is 1, 2, 3, 4.
words.ex_cn: 这些数字的顺序是1、2、3、4。
words.en: A sequence is a set of related events, movements, or items that follow each other in a particular order.

words.tr:
n. 顺序；条理；命令；订单；(生物学的)目；
v. 订购；命令；点餐；整理；
words.ex: The books are in alphabetical order.
words.ex_cn: 这些书是按字母顺序排列的。
words.en: If you order someone to do something, you tell them to do it in a way that they have to obey. Order can also refer to the way things are arranged or a request to make or supply something.

words.ex: He crushed the can with his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他用手把罐子压碎了。
words.en: To crush something means to press it very hard so that its shape is destroyed or so that it breaks into pieces. It can also mean to defeat someone completely, or to make someone feel extremely upset or disappointed.

words.tr:
n. 裂缝；噼啪声；
v. 破裂；
words.ex: There is a small crack in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有一条小裂缝。
words.en: If something hard cracks, or if you crack it, it becomes slightly damaged, with lines appearing on its surface.

words.ex: She ate a crisp apple for snack.
words.ex_cn: 她吃了一个脆苹果当点心。
words.en: Something that is crisp is hard, and makes a pleasant sound when you break it or crush it.

words.ex: He smashed the glass with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子把玻璃打碎了。
words.en: To break something into pieces violently and noisily, or to cause something to do this by dropping, throwing, or hitting it.

words.tr:
n. 代用品；代替物；
v. 替代；
words.ex: Honey is a good substitute for sugar.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是糖的良好代用品。
words.en: A substitute is something or someone that takes the place or function of another.

words.ex: He will replace the broken chair.
words.ex_cn: 他将代替这把坏掉的椅子。
words.en: If one thing or person replaces another, the first is used or acts instead of the second.

words.tr:
n. 供替代的选择；
adj. 供选择的；
words.ex: We need an alternative to this plan.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要这个计划的替代方案。
words.en: An alternative plan or method is one that you can use if you do not want to use another one.

words.ex: The hospital will isolate the patient to stop the spread.
words.ex_cn: 医院将隔离这名病人以防止传播。
words.en: To isolate someone or something means to separate them from other people or things, often in order to protect them or to prevent the spread of something harmful.

words.ex: His rude behavior alienated his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的行为使朋友们疏远了他。
words.en: To cause someone to feel isolated or estranged; to transfer the ownership of property to another.

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.ex: The defect in the phone made it hard to use.
words.ex_cn: 手机的缺陷让它很难使用。
words.en: A defect is a fault or imperfection in a person or thing.

words.ex: The flaw in the glass made it break easily.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃上的瑕疵让它很容易碎。
words.en: A flaw is a mistake or weakness in something that makes it less effective or valuable.

words.tr: v. 无法做到；失败；“fail”的现在分词； adj. 减弱中的； n. 失败；
words.ex: He was failing to finish the race.
words.ex_cn: 他没能完成比赛。
words.en: A failing is a fault or a weakness in someone's character or abilities.

words.ex: The disadvantage of living far away is long commute time.
words.ex_cn: 住得远的劣势是通勤时间长。
words.en: A disadvantage is a factor which makes someone or something less useful, acceptable, or successful than other people or things.

words.ex: The drawback of this phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的缺点是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A drawback is a feature of something that makes it less useful or desirable than it could be.

words.tr: n. 过错；故障；缺陷；断层；
words.ex: It was his fault that the car crashed.
words.ex_cn: 汽车撞车是他的过错。
words.en: A fault is a mistake or a weakness in something or someone.

words.ex: The painting showed a few small imperfections that the artist had missed.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画显示出艺术家忽略的几个小瑕疵。
words.en: An imperfection in something is a fault, weakness, or undesirable feature that it has.

words.ex: His weakness made him unable to fight back.
words.ex_cn: 他的软弱使他无法反击。
words.en: A weakness is a fault or lack of strength in someone's character or in a system, plan, or design.

words.ex: His main shortcoming is being late often.
words.ex_cn: 他的主要缺点是经常迟到。
words.en: A shortcoming is a fault or a failure to meet a certain standard, which means a person or thing is not as good as they should be.

words.ex: The inventive child made a toy from cardboard.
words.ex_cn: 这个有创造力的孩子用纸板做了一个玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as inventive, you mean that they are good at inventing things or have clever and original ideas.

words.tr: adj. 革新的；富有革新精神的；
words.ex: The company made an innovative phone.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司推出了一款革新的手机。
words.en: Something that is innovative is new and original, especially in the way that it is done.

words.ex: He is a creative boy who draws nice pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有创造力的男孩，会画漂亮的画。
words.en: Someone who is creative has the ability to invent and develop original ideas, especially in the arts.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.tr:
n. （长篇）小说；
adj. 新颖的；新奇的；
words.ex: He wrote a novel about a brave girl.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部关于一个勇敢女孩的小说。
words.en: A novel is a long written story about imaginary people and events.

words.tr: adj. 首创性的；先驱性的； v. “pioneer”的现在分词；
words.ex: He made a pioneering discovery in renewable energy.
words.ex_cn: 他在可再生能源领域做出了开创性的发现。
words.en: Involving new ideas or methods, and being the first to use them in a particular field.

words.ex: He stayed neutral in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: If you say that someone is neutral, you mean that they do not support or help either side in a disagreement, competition, or war.

words.ex: The judge gave an unbiased decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官作出了无偏见的判决。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unbiased, you mean they are fair and not likely to support one particular person or group involved in something.

words.tr:
adj. 客观的；
n. 目标；目的；
words.ex: He gave an objective opinion about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影给出了一个客观的看法。
words.en: An objective is something that you plan to do or achieve.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；不偏不倚的；
words.ex: The judge was impartial in the trial.
words.ex_cn: 法官在审判中是公正的。
words.en: Someone who is impartial is not directly involved in a particular situation, and is therefore able to give a fair opinion or decision about it.

words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件持客观态度。
words.en: If someone is disinterested in something, they have no personal involvement or investment in it and are therefore able to judge it fairly.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: The sentence has ambiguity because it can mean two things.
words.ex_cn: 这句话有歧义，因为它可以有两种意思。
words.en: If you say that there is ambiguity in something, you mean that it is unclear or confusing, or it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.tr: phrase. 非决定性的；不明确的；非最终的
words.ex: The test results are not definitive.
words.ex_cn: 测试结果不是决定性的。

words.ex: They communicate well with each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此沟通得很好。
words.en: To communicate means to share or exchange information, news, or ideas, especially by speaking or writing.

words.ex: The university conferred an honorary degree on him.
words.ex_cn: 大学授予他一个荣誉学位。
words.en: To confer something such as a degree or an honor on someone means to give it to them in a formal way. To confer with someone means to discuss something with them in order to make a decision.

words.ex: The number of apples corresponds to the number of oranges.
words.ex_cn: 苹果的数量与橙子的数量相对应。
words.en: If one thing corresponds to another, there is a close similarity or connection between them, often because one is the cause or the result of the other.

words.tr: v. 容纳；适应；为...提供住宿；
words.ex: The hotel can accommodate 200 guests.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店能容纳200位客人。
words.en: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

words.ex: He adapts to new rules quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快适应新规则。
words.en: If you adapt to a new situation or adapt yourself to it, you change your ideas or behaviour in order to deal with it successfully.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；持有；容纳；保留；举行；
n. 拿；控制；持；
words.ex: He held the rope tightly.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧抓住了绳子。
words.en: To have or keep in the hand; to maintain in a grasp; to keep in a specified state, relation, or position; to contain or be capable of containing; to have in one's possession; to keep back from action; to delay the action or effect of; to keep in custody; to bear, sustain, or support; to have or maintain in the mind; to consider or esteem; to assert or affirm; to organize and carry on; to have the ownership or use of; to keep from falling or moving; to remain unbroken or unyielding; to remain attached or faithful; to remain valid or effective.

words.ex: The food supply was inadequate for the number of people.
words.ex_cn: 食物供应对人数来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is inadequate, there is not enough of it or it is not good enough.

words.ex: The water supply is insufficient for the whole village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对整个村庄来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is insufficient, it is not enough for a particular purpose.

words.tr: adj. 不足的；缺乏的；有缺陷的
words.ex: The plant is deficient in sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物缺乏阳光。
words.en: If someone or something is deficient in a particular thing, they do not have the full amount of it that they need.

words.ex: He failed the test because of lack of sleep.
words.ex_cn: 他因为缺乏睡眠而考试不及格。
words.en: The state of being without or not having enough of something.

words.ex: We are short of money to buy food.
words.ex_cn: 我们缺钱买食物。
words.en: If you are short of something, you do not have enough of it. If something is short of a place, it is not as far as that place.

words.ex: He emphasizes the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 他强调作业的重要性。
words.en: To give special importance or prominence to (something) in speaking or writing.

words.tr:
n. 压力；强调；
v. 着重；强调；
words.ex: He feels stress from too much work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为工作太多而感到压力。
words.en: Stress is a state of mental or emotional strain or tension resulting from adverse or demanding circumstances.

words.tr:
v. 突出；强调；高光；
n. 最突出的部分；
words.ex: The teacher highlighted the key words in the text.
words.ex_cn: 老师把文中的关键词突出了。
words.en: To highlight something means to make it stand out or to emphasize it, often because it is important or interesting.

words.tr: phrase. 集中（精力；注意力等）于
words.ex: He focuses on his homework every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上专心做作业。
words.en: to direct your attention or effort towards something specific

words.tr: phrase. 集中于； 专心于
words.ex: He must concentrate on his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他必须专心做作业。
words.en: To direct all your attention and effort towards a particular activity, subject, or problem.

words.ex: He is skeptical about the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个新计划持怀疑态度。
words.en: If you are skeptical about something, you have doubts about it.

words.ex: He is sceptical about the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个新计划持怀疑态度。
words.en: If you are sceptical about something, you have doubts about it.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；怀疑的；拿不准的；
words.ex: The deal seemed dubious to me.
words.ex_cn: 这个交易在我看来很可疑。
words.en: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

words.tr: adj. 怀疑的；令人怀疑的；
words.ex: The police felt suspicious about the man's behavior.
words.ex_cn: 警察对这个人的行为感到怀疑。
words.en: If you are suspicious of someone or something, you do not trust them, and are careful when dealing with them.

words.tr: adj. 声名狼藉的；臭名昭著的；
words.ex: He is a notorious thief who stole from many stores.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个声名狼藉的小偷，偷过许多商店。
words.en: Someone or something that is notorious is well known for something bad.

words.tr: n. 恶名；坏名声；声名狼藉
words.ex: The criminal gained notoriety for his bold robberies.
words.ex_cn: 这名罪犯因大胆的抢劫而声名狼藉。
words.en: Notoriety is the state of being famous or well known for something bad.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；丑恶可耻的；公然的
words.ex: He made a flagrant mistake during the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中犯了一个明显的错误。
words.en: If you describe an action as flagrant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way and is intended to shock or offend people.

words.ex: The smelly trash made everyone cover their noses.
words.ex_cn: 那堆难闻的垃圾让每个人都捂住了鼻子。
words.en: Having a strong, unpleasant smell.

words.tr: adj. 有气味的；有臭气的
words.ex: The trash is odorous after being left in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾在阳光下放久了会有气味。
words.en: Having a distinctive smell, especially an unpleasant one.

words.ex: He speaks a local dialect in his village.
words.ex_cn: 他在村子里说一种地方方言。
words.en: A dialect is a form of a language that is spoken in a particular area and that uses some of its own words, grammar, and pronunciations.

words.ex: He speaks English with a French accent.
words.ex_cn: 他说英语时带有法国口音。
words.en: An accent is a distinctive way of pronouncing a language, especially one associated with a particular country, area, or social class.

words.ex: The car exceeded the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车超过了限速。
words.en: To be greater in quantity, degree, or intensity than something else.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.ex: The benefits outweigh the risks.
words.ex_cn: 好处超过了风险。
words.en: If one thing outweighs another, the first thing is of greater importance, benefit, or significance than the second thing.

words.ex: He is interested in linguistic patterns in children.
words.ex_cn: 他对儿童的语言模式感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to language or linguistics.

words.ex: She has a lingual talent for learning new languages.
words.ex_cn: 她有语言学习的天赋。
words.en: Relating to the tongue or language.

words.ex: He speaks English as his first language.
words.ex_cn: 他说英语作为他的第一语言。
words.en: Language is the system of communication in speech and writing that is used by people of a particular country or area.

words.tr: adj. 两种语言的；用两种语言的；
words.ex: He is a bilingual student who speaks English and Spanish.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个会说英语和西班牙语的双语学生。
words.en: A bilingual person is someone who can speak two languages equally well.

words.ex: The school values diversity in its students.
words.ex_cn: 学校重视学生的多样性。
words.en: The state of being diverse; variety.

words.tr: n. （同一事物）不同种类；多样性；（动植物的）品种；变化；
words.ex: The store sells a variety of apples.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售各种各样的苹果。
words.en: If something has variety, it consists of things which are different from each other.

words.tr: adj. 范围广阔的；内容广泛的
words.ex: He has wide-ranging interests in science and art.
words.ex_cn: 他对科学和艺术有广泛的兴趣。
words.en: Covering a wide range of subjects or topics.

words.tr: adj. 混合的；混杂的； v. 混合；“mix”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He ate a mixed salad with tomatoes and cucumbers.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一份混合沙拉，里面有番茄和黄瓜。
words.en: If something is mixed, it consists of different things or people.

words.tr:
v. 交配繁殖；饲养；
n. 品种；
words.ex: The farmers breed cows to get more milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民让奶牛交配繁殖以获得更多牛奶。
words.en: If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.

words.ex: This forest has many different species of birds.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林有多种不同的鸟类物种。
words.en: A species is a class of plants or animals whose members have the same main characteristics and are able to breed with each other.

words.ex: The main criterion for winning is fairness.
words.ex_cn: 获胜的主要标准是公平。
words.en: A criterion is a principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

words.ex: He begins his homework after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后开始做作业。
words.en: To start doing something; to take the first step into a process or activity.

words.tr:
v. 发射；发起；启动；
n. 发射；投掷；启动；
words.ex: They will launch a rocket tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将发射一枚火箭。
words.en: To launch something means to send it into the air, space, or water, especially with a lot of force or effort, or to start an activity, event, or project.

words.tr:
adj. 最初的；开始的；
n. 首字母；
words.ex: This is the initial plan for the project.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个项目的最初计划。
words.en: The first letter of a name or word, used to represent the whole name or word.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.tr: n. 倡议；主动权；自发性；措施；
words.ex: The school launched an initiative to reduce plastic use.
words.ex_cn: 学校发起了一项减少塑料使用的倡议。
words.en: An initiative is an important act or statement that is intended to solve a problem.

words.ex: The origin of this tradition is unknown.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统的起源不明。
words.en: The origin of something is the point or place where it begins, or the cause from which it arises.

words.tr: adj. 拙劣的；贫穷的；缺少的；可怜的；
words.ex: The acting in that movie was poor.
words.ex_cn: 那部电影的表演很拙劣。
words.en: If you describe someone as poor, you mean that they do not have enough money to live on or that they have very little money.

words.tr: phrase. phr. 处于贫困之中；生活贫困
words.ex: Many families in this region live in poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区的许多家庭生活在贫困中。
words.en: Living in a state of being extremely poor.

words.tr: adj. 穷困的；赤穷的；贫瘠的； v. “impoverish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The impoverished family lived in a small house with no heating.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫困的家庭住在一个没有暖气的小房子里。
words.en: An impoverished person or area is very poor.

words.tr: adj. 不平常的；不寻常的；
words.ex: It is unusual to see snow in this city.
words.ex_cn: 在这个城市看到雪是不平常的。
words.en: If something is unusual, it does not happen very often or you do not see it or hear it very often.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.ex: The mountain has great prominence in the landscape.
words.ex_cn: 这座山在景观中十分突出。
words.en: If someone or something is in a position of prominence, they are important or well-known.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；尚未处理的；
words.ex: He is an outstanding student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名杰出的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

words.tr: v. 区分；“distinguish”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 卓越的；著名的；
words.ex: He distinguished the fake coin from the real one.
words.ex_cn: 他把假硬币和真硬币区分开来。
words.en: If you describe a person or their work as distinguished, you mean that they have been very successful in their career and have a good reputation.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.ex: He is a man of great eminence in science.
words.ex_cn: 他在科学界享有很高的声望。
words.en: Eminence refers to a position of great distinction or superiority, especially in a particular field or profession.

words.ex: He uses deductive reasoning to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他使用演绎推理来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Deductive reasoning is a logical process in which a conclusion is based on the concordance of multiple premises that are generally assumed to be true.

words.ex: He uses inferential statistics to predict the result.
words.ex_cn: 他使用推断统计来预测结果。
words.en: Inferential means relating to or involving inference, which is the process of deriving logical conclusions from premises known or assumed to be true.

words.tr: adj. 诱导的；归纳的；感应的
words.ex: The scientist used inductive reasoning to form a hypothesis.
words.ex_cn: 科学家使用归纳推理来形成一个假设。
words.en: Inductive reasoning involves making broad generalizations from specific observations.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.ex: He can deduce the answer from the clues.
words.ex_cn: 他能从线索中推断出答案。
words.en: If you deduce something or deduce that something is true, you reach that conclusion because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: The induction of the new mayor will be held next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新市长的就职典礼将在下周一举行。
words.en: Induction is the process or action of inducting someone to a position or organization, or the process of reasoning from specific cases to general rules.

words.tr:
adj. 令人困惑的；使人糊涂的
v. 使迷惑；使昏乱；“bewilder”的现在分词
words.ex: The maze was bewildering.
words.ex_cn: 这个迷宫令人困惑。
words.en: If something is bewildering, it is very confusing and difficult to understand or to make a decision about.

words.tr: adj. 令人困惑不解的； v. “puzzle”的现在分词；
words.ex: The puzzle was puzzling even for experts.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜题即使对专家来说也令人困惑不解。
words.en: If something is puzzling, it is difficult to understand or explain because it is not clear or is confusing.

words.ex: The puzzle was perplexing and hard to solve.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜题令人困惑，很难解决。
words.en: If you find something perplexing, you find it confusing or difficult to understand.

words.ex: The government subsidize small businesses to help them grow.
words.ex_cn: 政府资助小企业以帮助它们发展。
words.en: To subsidize something means to pay part of the cost of it, usually as a way of helping people or organizations that cannot afford to pay the full cost themselves.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.tr:
v. 帮助；
n. 帮助；
words.ex: He helps his sister with her homework.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助妹妹做作业。
words.en: If you help someone, you make it easier for them to do something, for example by doing part of the work for them or by giving them advice or information.

words.tr:
n. 金融；财务；
v. 提供资金；
words.ex: He works in finance in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他在纽约从事金融工作。
words.en: Finance is the management of large amounts of money, especially by governments or large companies.

words.ex: The government gives a subsidy to farmers.
words.ex_cn: 政府向农民提供补贴。
words.en: A subsidy is money that is paid by a government or other authority in order to help an industry or business, or to pay for a public service.

words.ex: There is plenty of food on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌上有很多食物。
words.en: A large quantity or number; more than enough.

words.ex: He spends a great deal of time on homework.
words.ex_cn: 他花大量时间做作业。
words.en: A large amount or quantity of something.

words.ex: He has a lot of books.
words.ex_cn: 他有很多书。
words.en: A large number or amount of something.

words.ex: There is ample food for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有足够的食物。
words.en: If there is an ample amount of something, there is enough of it and usually some extra.

words.ex: We have sufficient food for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们有足够的食物用于这次旅行。
words.en: If something is sufficient for a particular purpose, there is enough of it for the purpose.

words.ex: The water supply is adequate for the village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对这个村庄来说是足够的。
words.en: If something is adequate, there is enough of it or it is good enough to be used or accepted.

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.ex: The elephant is enormous.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象非常巨大。
words.en: If you describe something as enormous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size or amount.

words.ex: The mountain is immense.
words.ex_cn: 这座山非常巨大。
words.en: Extremely large or great, especially in scale or degree.

words.ex: There are numerous books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书架上有许多书。
words.en: If people or things are numerous, they exist or are present in large numbers.

words.ex: This phone is outdated and doesn't work well.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机过时了，用起来不好。
words.en: If you describe something as outdated, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；老式的； v. “outmode”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This phone is outmoded and needs to be replaced.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，需要更换。
words.en: If you describe something as outmoded, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.tr: adj. 老式的；老派的；守旧的
words.ex: He wears an old-fashioned hat.
words.ex_cn: 他戴着一顶过时的帽子。
words.en: If you describe something as old-fashioned, you mean that it is no longer modern, current, or fashionable.

words.ex: This phone is out of date.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机过时了。
words.en: No longer fashionable or current; obsolete.

words.tr: v. 追溯到；“date”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 过时的；陈旧的；
words.ex: This coin is dated to the year 1500.
words.ex_cn: 这枚硬币追溯到1500年。
words.en: Something that is dated is old-fashioned and no longer relevant or useful.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.ex: The joy was transitory, and soon he felt sad again.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是暂时的，不久他又感到悲伤了。
words.en: Something that is transitory lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.tr: adj. 短命的；持续不久的；昙花一现的
words.ex: The fashion trend was short-lived.
words.ex_cn: 这种时尚潮流是短暂的。
words.en: Something that is short-lived does not last very long.

words.ex: He did a preliminary test before the main experiment.
words.ex_cn: 他在主要实验之前做了一个初步测试。
words.en: Preliminary means something that is done or happens before the main part or event, especially as an introduction or preparation.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；小学的；初等的；原来的；最初的；
words.ex: Primary goal is to stay safe.
words.ex_cn: 首要目标是保持安全。
words.en: Something that is primary is more important than anything else.

words.ex: This bag is durable and lasts for years.
words.ex_cn: 这个包很耐用，可以用很多年。
words.en: Something that is durable is strong and lasts a long time without breaking or becoming weaker.

words.tr: phrase. 耐磨；能够承受磨损
words.ex: This fabric is able to stand wear.
words.ex_cn: 这种布料耐磨。

words.ex: This battery can last a long time.
words.ex_cn: 这种电池可以持续很长时间。
words.en: Endure or persist for an extended period without failing or diminishing.

words.tr: phrase. 一次又一次；屡次；反复地
words.ex: He fails time after time, but he never gives up.
words.ex_cn: 他一次又一次失败，但他从不放弃。
words.en: If you say that something happens time after time, you mean that it happens often and usually that it is annoying or that it causes problems.

words.tr: phrase. 再三地；反复不止地
words.ex: He tried again and again to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他一遍又一遍地尝试解决这个问题。
words.en: Repeatedly; many times.

words.ex: He often goes to the park after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后常常去公园。
words.en: Many times; frequently.

words.ex: He frequently visits his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他经常去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: If something happens frequently, it happens often.

words.ex: He repeatedly asked for help.
words.ex_cn: 他再三地请求帮助。
words.en: If something is done repeatedly, it is done again and again.

words.ex: The aforementioned rules apply to all students.
words.ex_cn: 前述的规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: Used to refer to something that has already been mentioned.

words.ex: The aforesaid rule applies to all students.
words.ex_cn: 上述规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: Used to refer to something that has already been mentioned.

words.ex: He is a former teacher who now works as a writer.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名以前的老师，现在是一名作家。
words.en: Former is used to describe someone who used to have a particular job, position, or role, but no longer has it.

words.ex: The rules mentioned above are important.
words.ex_cn: 上面提到的规则很重要。

words.ex: Young people like to use smartphones.
words.ex_cn: 年轻人喜欢使用智能手机。
words.en: Young people are individuals in the early stages of life, typically characterized by their energy, potential, and the challenges they face in growing up.

words.ex: The youngster rode his bike to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个年轻人每天骑自行车去上学。
words.en: A youngster is a young person, especially a child or teenager.

words.ex: He misses his youth when he played football every day.
words.ex_cn: 他怀念每天踢足球的青春时光。
words.en: The period of your life when you are young, or the state of being young.

words.tr: phrase. 年轻成年人（通常指18至35岁之间的成年人）
words.ex: He is a young adult who works at a bookstore.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名在书店工作的年轻人。
words.en: A young adult is a person who is in the early stages of adulthood, typically between the ages of 18 and 30.

words.tr:
n. 青少年；
adj. 青少年的；
words.ex: The adolescent walked to school with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 这个青少年和朋友们一起走路去上学。
words.en: An adolescent is a young person who is developing into an adult.

words.tr: phrase. 青少年（时期）的；青少年群体（的）
words.ex: The teenage years are important for growth.
words.ex_cn: 青少年时期对成长很重要。

words.ex: The stars seem eternal in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中的星星看起来是永久的。
words.en: If something is eternal, it lasts forever.

words.tr: adj. 永久的；永恒的；经久不变的
words.ex: The love between them is everlasting.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的爱是永恒的。
words.en: Something that is everlasting lasts forever or for a very long time.

words.ex: I will love you forever.
words.ex_cn: 我会永远爱你。
words.en: If you say that something will happen or continue forever, you mean that it will always happen or continue.

words.ex: The desert seems endless.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠看起来无穷无尽。
words.en: If you say that something is endless, you mean that it is very large or lasts for a very long time, and it seems as if it will never stop.

words.ex: He made a permanent change to his lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的生活方式做出了永久的改变。
words.en: Something that is permanent exists or happens all the time, or exists for a long time without changing.

words.ex: The machine makes a perpetual noise.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发出持续的噪音。
words.en: Something that is perpetual continues indefinitely or for a very long time without interruption.

words.tr: phrase. 持续终生的；终身的
words.ex: This is a lasting throughout life commitment.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个持续终生的承诺。

words.ex: I eat ice cream once in a while.
words.ex_cn: 我偶尔吃冰淇淋。
words.en: Occasionally; from time to time.

words.ex: He visits his grandparents from time to time.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: If you do something from time to time, you do it occasionally but not regularly.

words.ex: He visits his grandparents now and then.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: Occasionally; from time to time.

words.ex: He is late at times.
words.ex_cn: 他有时会迟到。
words.en: on some occasions; occasionally

words.ex: I occasionally walk my dog in the park.
words.ex_cn: 我偶尔在公园遛狗。
words.en: If something happens occasionally, it happens sometimes, but not regularly or often.

words.tr:
n. 申斥；谴责
v. 斥责；训斥
words.ex: The teacher gave him a reprimand for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而训斥了他。
words.en: A reprimand is a formal or official expression of disapproval, typically by a person in authority.

words.ex: My mother chides me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈因为我回家晚而责备我。
words.en: If you chide someone, you speak to them angrily because they have done something wrong.

words.ex: My mom scolded me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈因为我回家晚而责备了我。
words.en: If you scold someone, you speak angrily to them because they have done something wrong.

words.ex: The teacher reproved the student for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而责骂了他。
words.en: If you reprove someone, you speak angrily or seriously to them because they have behaved in a wrong or foolish way.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: He often criticizes his brother for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他经常批评他弟弟迟到。
words.en: If you criticize someone or something, you express your disapproval of them by saying what you think is wrong with them.

words.tr:
n. 责任；责备；
v. 责怪；归咎于；
words.ex: He took the blame for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他承担了这个错误的责任。
words.en: If you blame a person or thing for something bad, you believe or say that they are responsible for it or that they caused it.

words.ex: He always tries to find fault with his classmates' work.
words.ex_cn: 他总是试图挑他同学作业的毛病。
words.en: To criticize someone or something, often unfairly and too much.

words.tr:
v. 支持；支撑；
n. 拥护；帮助；
words.ex: My friends support me when I feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 当我感到难过时，我的朋友们支持我。
words.en: If you support someone or their ideas or aims, you agree with them, and perhaps help them because you want them to succeed.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.ex: My friend always backs up my ideas in meetings.
words.ex_cn: 我的朋友总是在会议上支持我的想法。
words.en: To support someone or something; to make a copy of computer data to protect against loss.

words.ex: The judge will uphold the law.
words.ex_cn: 法官将维护法律。
words.en: If you uphold something such as a law, a principle, or a decision, you support and maintain it.

words.tr: adj. 搞错的；弄错的；误解的； v. “mistake”的过去分词；
words.ex: He was mistaken about the time of the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他对会议的时间搞错了。
words.en: If you are mistaken about something, you are wrong about it.

words.ex: His answer was erroneous because he added wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案是错误的，因为他加错了。
words.en: If you describe someone's beliefs or opinions as erroneous, you mean that they are incorrect and based on false information.

words.tr: adj. 错误的；不正确的；不当的；
words.ex: The answer is wrong.
words.ex_cn: 这个答案是错误的。
words.en: If you say there is something wrong, you mean there is something unsatisfactory about the situation, person, or thing you are talking about.

words.ex: The answer is incorrect.
words.ex_cn: 这个答案是不正确的。
words.en: If something is incorrect, it is not accurate or true.

words.ex: The news was false.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻是虚假的。
words.en: If something is false, it is incorrect, untrue, or mistaken.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.ex: He composes music in his spare time.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间创作音乐。
words.en: To compose something means to make it by combining parts or elements.

words.ex: The team comprises five players and one coach.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队包括五名球员和一名教练。
words.en: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.

words.ex: The old bridge will disintegrate if no one fixes it.
words.ex_cn: 如果没人修理，这座旧桥会瓦解。
words.en: If something disintegrates, it breaks into many small pieces or parts and is destroyed.

words.ex: The apple will decompose in the soil.
words.ex_cn: 苹果会在土壤中分解。
words.en: If something decomposes, or if it is decomposed, it decays or breaks down into smaller parts or substances.

words.tr: phrase. 打碎；分裂；解体；结束；期终放假
words.ex: He broke up the ice with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子把冰打碎了。
words.en: To end a relationship or to disintegrate into pieces.

words.ex: Please separate the cake into small parts.
words.ex_cn: 请把蛋糕分成小部分。

words.ex: He asked for her consent before starting the project.
words.ex_cn: 他在开始这个项目之前征求了她的同意。
words.en: Consent is permission for something to happen or agreement to do something.

words.ex: The team was unanimous in choosing the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 团队在选择新领导时意见完全一致。
words.en: When a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 正确的；合适的；正当的；
words.ex: This is the proper way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是解决这个问题的正确方法。
words.en: If something is proper, it is suitable or correct for a particular purpose, situation, or person.

words.ex: This shirt is suitable for the party.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫适合这场派对。
words.en: Something that is suitable for a particular person or thing is right or acceptable for them.

words.ex: Wearing shorts to the meeting is inappropriate.
words.ex_cn: 穿短裤去参加会议是不合适的。
words.en: If you say that something is inappropriate, you are criticizing it because you think it is not suitable for a particular situation or purpose.

words.tr: adj. 不适当的；不正当的；不成体统的
words.ex: Wearing shorts to the meeting is improper.
words.ex_cn: 穿短裤去开会是不适当的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as improper, you mean that it is rude or shocking.

words.tr: adj. 不适宜的；不合适的；
words.ex: This shirt is unsuitable for the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫不适合寒冷的天气。
words.en: If someone or something is unsuitable for a particular purpose or situation, they are not appropriate for it.

words.ex: Eating vegetables is good for your health.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜对你的健康有好处。
words.en: To be beneficial or advantageous for someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 有助益的；起作用的

words.ex: He gave a meaningful speech that helped many people.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一次有意义的演讲，帮助了很多人。
words.en: If you describe something as meaningful, you mean that it is important, serious, or useful in some way.

words.tr: phrase. 心态；心情；精神状态
words.ex: He is in a good frame of mind today.
words.ex_cn: 他今天心情很好。
words.en: A particular mood that influences your attitudes or behaviour.

words.ex: His mind set makes him refuse new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他的思维定式让他拒绝新想法。

words.tr: phrase. 一个人正在思考的方式；思维方式
words.ex: He explained the way one is thinking about the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他解释了一个人正在思考问题的方式。

words.ex: Can you clarify your answer?
words.ex_cn: 你能澄清一下你的答案吗？
words.en: To clarify something means to make it easier to understand by explaining it more clearly.

words.ex: Please make clear your answer so everyone can understand.
words.ex_cn: 请把你的答案说清楚，以便每个人都能理解。
words.en: To make something understood or known in a way that is unambiguous.

words.ex: He chooses coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都选择喝咖啡。
words.en: To choose means to select someone or something from a group of possibilities.

words.ex: They elect a new president every four years.
words.ex_cn: 他们每四年选举一位新总统。
words.en: To choose someone for a particular job or position by voting.

words.ex: He will opt for tea instead of coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他会选择茶而不是咖啡。
words.en: To choose one thing or one course of action in preference to others.

words.ex: I pick the red shirt for the party.
words.ex_cn: 我为派对选择红色衬衫。
words.en: To choose something from a group of things or people, or to remove something from a place using your fingers or a tool.

words.ex: The teacher singled out one student for praise.
words.ex_cn: 老师挑出一名学生进行表扬。
words.en: To choose someone or something from a group for special attention or treatment.

words.tr:
v. 使用；利用；
n. 使用；用途；
words.ex: I use a pen to write.
words.ex_cn: 我用笔写字。
words.en: If you use something, you do something with it in order to do a job or to achieve a particular result or effect.

words.ex: He took advantage of the free tickets.
words.ex_cn: 他利用了免费的票。
words.en: To use a particular situation to do or get what you want.

words.tr: phrase. 没有效果；无济于事
phrase. 徒劳的；白费的；没有结果的
words.ex: He tried to fix the car, but it was in vain.
words.ex_cn: 他试图修理汽车，但徒劳无功。
words.en: Without success or result; futile.

words.tr: adv. 显然；表面上看起来；
words.ex: He is apparently late for the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他显然迟到了会议。
words.en: You use apparently to indicate that the information you are giving is something that you have heard, but you are not certain that it is true.

words.ex: He is patently lying about his age.
words.ex_cn: 他明显在谎报自己的年龄。
words.en: In a way that is clear and obvious to anyone.

words.ex: He obviously forgot his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他显然忘了做作业。
words.en: in a way that is easily perceived or understood; clearly.

words.ex: He is evidently tired after the long walk.
words.ex_cn: 他走完漫长的路后显然很累。
words.en: In a way that is clearly seen or understood; obviously.

words.ex: He brags about his new car every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都吹嘘自己的新车。
words.en: To speak boastfully or with excessive pride about one's achievements or possessions.

words.tr: phrase. 吹嘘；自夸（关于某事）
words.ex: He boasts about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他吹嘘自己的新车。
words.en: If someone boasts about something that they have done or that they own, they talk about it very proudly, often in a way that other people find annoying.

words.ex: He likes to show off his new bike.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢炫耀他的新自行车。
words.en: If someone shows off, they behave in a way that is intended to attract attention and impress people, often by displaying their abilities or possessions.

words.tr: phrase. 过分夸奖；对...评价过高
words.ex: I think you speak too highly of your friend.
words.ex_cn: 我觉得你过分夸奖你的朋友了。

words.ex: He can identify the bird by its song.
words.ex_cn: 他能通过鸟的叫声识别它。
words.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

words.ex: I recognize her face from school.
words.ex_cn: 我从学校认出了她的脸。
words.en: If you recognize someone or something, you know who or what they are because you have seen or heard them before.

words.ex: Please get in touch with me if you have questions.
words.ex_cn: 如果你有问题，请与我联系。
words.en: To make contact or communicate with someone.

words.ex: He tried to contact with his old friend by phone.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过电话与他的老朋友联系。
words.en: Physical or communicative interaction with someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 相当于；等于；与…有同等作用
words.ex: Two plus two is equivalent to four.
words.ex_cn: 二加二等于四。
words.en: If one thing is equivalent to another, they have the same value, purpose, qualities, etc.

words.tr:
adj. 相等的；同等的；
v. 等于；比得上；
words.ex: Two plus two is equal to four.
words.ex_cn: 二加二等于四。
words.en: If two things are equal, or if one thing is equal to another, they are the same in size, number, standard, or value.

words.tr: v. 兑现；递送；交付；发表；为…接生；
words.ex: He promised to deliver on his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺要兑现自己的目标。
words.en: To bring and hand over (a letter, parcel, or ordered goods) to the proper recipient or address.

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.tr:
v. 派遣；调遣；发送
n. 快信；发送；派遣
words.ex: He will dispatch the package tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会寄出这个包裹。
words.en: To send someone or something to a particular place for a particular purpose.

words.tr: phrase. 分发；发出；发表；用尽
words.ex: He gives out books to the students.
words.ex_cn: 他把书分发给学生们。
words.en: To distribute or hand out something; to emit or produce something such as a sound or smell; to announce or make something known publicly.

words.ex: He will hand over the keys tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会交出钥匙。
words.en: To give something to someone else, especially because you have been ordered to do so or because it is necessary.

words.ex: We took a detour to avoid the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们绕道以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A detour is a longer, less direct way to go somewhere, used to avoid a problem or to visit something along the way.

words.tr: phrase. 绕路；绕远路；采取迂回的方式
words.ex: We decided to take a roundabout way to avoid traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定绕路以避开交通堵塞。

words.tr: phrase. 被禁止做某事；被阻止做某事

words.ex: He was banned from entering the club after causing a disturbance.
words.ex_cn: v. 他因引起骚乱而被禁止进入俱乐部。
words.en: To be officially prohibited from doing something.

words.tr:
n. 结果；
v. 导致；
words.ex: The result of the test was good.
words.ex_cn: 这次测试的结果很好。
words.en: A consequence, outcome, or effect of an action or situation.

words.ex: The aftermath of the storm left many trees down.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，许多树被吹倒了。
words.en: The aftermath of an important event, especially a harmful one, is the situation that results from it.

words.ex: Lying has serious consequences.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎会有严重的后果。
words.en: A consequence is a result or effect of an action or condition.

words.tr: phrase. 轻视；贬低；不放在眼里；对…不重视
words.ex: He made little of his success, saying it was just luck.
words.ex_cn: 他轻描淡写自己的成功，说那只是运气。
words.en: To treat something as unimportant or to minimize its significance.

words.ex: He overlooked the mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了报告中的错误。
words.en: If you overlook a fact or problem, you do not notice it, or do not realize how important it is.

words.ex: He ignored the warning sign.
words.ex_cn: 他忽视了警告标志。
words.en: If you ignore someone or something, you pay no attention to them.

words.ex: His neglect of the project caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 他对项目的疏忽导致了延误。
words.en: If you neglect someone or something, you fail to give them the attention or care that they need.

words.tr:
n. 漠视；忽视；
v. 漠视；不理会；不顾；
words.ex: His advice was met with disregard.
words.ex_cn: 他的建议遭到了漠视。
words.en: If you disregard something, you ignore it or do not take account of it.

words.tr: phrase. 几乎不关心；很少在意
words.ex: They give little care to the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他们几乎不关心规则。

words.tr: phrase. 失灵的；出故障的；不按顺序的；不合规矩的
words.ex: The printer is out of order.
words.ex_cn: 打印机坏了。
words.en: To not be working correctly or to be broken; to behave inappropriately or against the rules.

words.ex: He avoids eating sugar to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃糖以保持健康。
words.en: If you avoid something, you take action in order to prevent it from happening to you.

words.ex: He shuns loud parties because he is shy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为害羞而避开热闹的派对。
words.en: If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

words.tr: phrase. 避免；绕开；说服；顺利应付
words.ex: He tried to get around the rules by using a loophole.
words.ex_cn: 他试图利用一个漏洞来规避规则。
words.en: To find a way to deal with or avoid a problem; to move or travel from place to place; to become known by many people.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.ex: He left a heap of clothes on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把一堆衣服扔在地上。
words.en: A heap of things is a pile of them, especially a pile arranged in a rather untidy way.

words.ex: Books are piling up on the table.
words.ex_cn: 书正堆在桌子上。
words.en: If things pile up, they gradually increase in number or amount until there is a large quantity of them.

words.ex: He cleaned the floor by means of a mop.
words.ex_cn: 他用拖把打扫了地板。
words.en: If you do something by means of a particular method, instrument, or process, you do it using that method, instrument, or process.

words.ex: He passed the test by virtue of his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他凭借努力学习通过了考试。
words.en: Because of or as a result of something.

words.ex: He solved the problem by the use of a calculator.
words.ex_cn: 他通过使用计算器解决了这个问题。

words.tr: phrase. 区分，辨别……之间的不同
words.ex: It's important to distinguish between fact and opinion.
words.ex_cn: 重要的是要区分事实和观点。
words.en: To recognize or understand the difference between two or more things or people.

words.ex: You should make a distinction between good and bad.
words.ex_cn: 你应该区分好与坏。

words.tr: phrase. 区分 A 与 B；辨别 A 和 B
words.ex: It's difficult to tell A from B in this low light.
words.ex_cn: 在这么暗的光线下很难区分A和B。
words.en: To distinguish or differentiate one thing from another.

words.ex: He deserves a break after working so hard.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作后值得休息一下。
words.en: If you say that a person or thing deserves something, you mean that they should have it or receive it because of their actions or qualities.

words.ex: Every child has right to go to school.
words.ex_cn: 每个孩子都有权上学。

words.ex: Your hard work is worthy of praise.
words.ex_cn: 你的辛勤工作值得表扬。

words.ex: I can count on my brother to help me.
words.ex_cn: 我可以依靠我哥哥帮我。
words.en: If you count on someone or something, you rely on them to support you or help you.

words.ex: He depends on his brother for help.
words.ex_cn: 他依靠他哥哥帮忙。
words.en: To rely on someone or something for support, help, or supply; to be determined or influenced by something.

words.ex: He relies on his brother for help.
words.ex_cn: 他依靠弟弟帮忙。
words.en: To depend on with full trust or confidence.

words.tr: phrase. 依靠；搁在；停留在；基于
words.ex: The bridge must rest on strong pillars.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥必须依靠坚固的支柱。
words.en: To depend or rely on something for support or as a basis.

words.ex: The decision is based on facts.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定基于事实。
words.en: To use something as the foundation or starting point for something else.

words.ex: We need to settle on a date for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要选定一个旅行的日期。
words.en: To decide on something after considering it carefully.

words.tr: phrase. v. 为……做好准备；挺住以应对
words.ex: He braces for the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他为风暴做好准备。
words.en: To prepare yourself for something difficult or unpleasant.

words.ex: He prepares for the test every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上为考试做准备。
words.en: To make ready or get set for a future event or situation.

words.ex: It was the critical moment of the game.
words.ex_cn: 那是比赛的关键时刻。

words.ex: Water is vital for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

words.ex: It is important to eat healthy food.
words.ex_cn: 吃健康的食物很重要。
words.en: Something that is important is very significant, is highly valued, or is necessary.

words.ex: His decisive action saved the team.
words.ex_cn: 他果断的行动拯救了团队。
words.en: If a fact, action, or event is decisive, it makes it certain that there will be a particular result.

words.ex: This decision is pivotal for the company's future.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来至关重要。
words.en: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else.

words.ex: I consider going to the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我考虑明天去公园。
words.en: If you consider something, you think about it carefully.

words.ex: Please take into consideration the weather before we go out.
words.ex_cn: 在我们出去之前，请考虑一下天气。
words.en: To think about and include a particular thing or fact when you are forming an opinion or making a decision.

words.ex: The teacher took into account his effort, not just his grade.
words.ex_cn: 老师重视他的努力，而不仅仅是他的分数。
words.en: To consider or remember something when judging a situation.

words.ex: He omitted the last word in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他省略了句子中的最后一个词。
words.en: If you omit something, you do not include it in an activity or piece of work, deliberately or accidentally.

words.tr: phrase. 不包括；不计；把……除外
words.ex: The price is $50, exclusive of tax.
words.ex_cn: 价格是50美元，不含税。
words.en: Not including; excluding.

words.ex: Not counting the weekend, there are five days left.
words.ex_cn: 不包括周末，还剩五天。

words.tr: phrase. 遗漏；省略；排除在外
words.ex: He is leaving out the important details.
words.ex_cn: 他正在漏掉重要的细节。
words.en: Omitting or excluding something, often unintentionally.

words.ex: The child loves to play with fantasy stories about dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子喜欢玩关于龙的幻想故事。
words.en: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you imagine, which is unlikely to happen.

words.ex: Children have a strong imagination.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们有很强的想象力。
words.en: The ability to form pictures or ideas in your mind of things that are new and exciting, or not real.

words.ex: He stayed calm in the face of danger.
words.ex_cn: 他在危险面前保持冷静。
words.en: If you do something in the face of a particular situation, you do it despite the difficulties or problems that the situation causes.

words.tr: phrase. 在…面前；当着…的面；有…在场时
words.ex: He stayed quiet in the presence of his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他在老师面前保持安静。
words.en: When you are in the presence of someone or something, you are in the same place as them and they are there with you.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 面对；使面对（问题、挑战等）；使对质
words.ex: He must confront with his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: To face someone or something in a way that is aggressive or challenging.

words.ex: We must face to the problem.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须面对这个问题。

words.tr: phrase. 消除；终止；废除；杀死；干掉
words.ex: They want to do away with the old rules.
words.ex_cn: 他们想废除旧规则。
words.en: To do away with something means to get rid of it or to stop using it.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.ex: Please remove the trash from the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 请把厨房的垃圾去掉。
words.en: To take something or someone away from a place or off a surface.

words.ex: He wants to get rid of the old chair.
words.ex_cn: 他想扔掉那把旧椅子。
words.en: To dispose of or remove something unwanted or undesirable.

words.ex: He left early, according to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 根据老师的说法，他早早离开了。
words.en: In accordance with or as stated by something.

words.tr: phrase. 以...为基础；根据；按照
words.ex: He made a decision on the basis of the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他基于事实做出了决定。
words.en: On the basis of means using something as the foundation or starting point for something else.

words.tr: phrase. 以……为理由；根据；基于
words.ex: He was fired on the ground of poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 他因表现不佳而被解雇。
words.en: Because of; on the basis of.

words.ex: He changed his mind in the light of new facts.
words.ex_cn: 根据新事实，他改变了主意。
words.en: If you do or decide something in the light of something else, you do it or decide it after considering that thing.

words.tr: phrase. 符合；一致；与…成一直线
words.ex: His decision is in line with the company's rules.
words.ex_cn: 他的决定符合公司的规定。
words.en: In agreement or conformity with something.

words.ex: He acted in accordance with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他按照规则行事。
words.en: If something is done in accordance with a particular rule or system, it is done in the way that the rule or system says that it should be done.

words.tr: phrase. 就...而言；在...方面；根据
words.ex: In terms of cost, this phone is cheaper.
words.ex_cn: 从成本来看，这部手机更便宜。
words.en: used to indicate what aspect of a subject you are talking about

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.tr:
adj. 极度的；
n. 极端；极端的事物；
words.ex: He felt extreme pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后感到极度疼痛。
words.en: If you describe something as extreme, you mean that it is very great in degree or intensity.

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.ex: They will carry out the experiment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将进行这个实验。
words.en: To perform or complete a task, duty, or project.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.ex: He finally realize his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于意识到自己的错误。
words.en: If you realize that something is true, you become aware of that fact or understand it.

words.ex: Her dream made come true.
words.ex_cn: 她的梦想实现了。

words.ex: I ate my sandwich, and the rest I gave to my dog.
words.ex_cn: 我吃了我的三明治，剩下的给了我的狗。
words.en: The remaining part of something.

words.tr: phrase. 剩余部分；余数；其余的人或物
words.ex: The remainder is two when you divide eight by three.
words.ex_cn: 八除以三的余数是二。
words.en: The part that remains or is left over after the rest has been used, taken, or considered.

words.tr:
adj. 剩余的；
n. 残留物；
words.ex: We ate the leftover food for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 我们早餐吃了剩下的食物。
words.en: Remaining after the rest has been used, consumed, or dealt with.

words.tr: n. 优势；有利条件；好处；
words.ex: His height gives him an advantage in basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他的身高在篮球中给了他优势。
words.en: An advantage is a factor or circumstance that puts you in a favorable or superior position.

words.ex: His strength helped him lift the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他的力量让他举起了那个重箱子。
words.en: The quality or state of being physically strong.

words.tr: phrase. 长处; 特长; 强点
words.ex: His strong point is solving math problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他的强项是快速解决数学问题。
words.en: A strong point is a particular skill or ability that someone has which gives them an advantage.

words.tr:
v. 有益于；有助于；
n. 利益；好处；
words.ex: Exercise benefits your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼有益于你的健康。
