words.en: A benefit is something that helps you or improves your life in some way.

words.ex: The merit of this plan is its simplicity.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划的优点是简单。
words.en: If something has merit, it has good or worthwhile qualities.

words.ex: Honesty is a great virtue.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种伟大的美德。
words.en: A virtue is a good quality or way of behaving.

words.ex: She had only the faintest inkling of what he was planning.
words.ex_cn: 她对他正在策划的事情只有一点模糊的概念。
words.en: An inkling is a slight knowledge or suspicion of something.

words.tr: n. 暗示；提示；有益的建议；
words.ex: He gave me a hint about the surprise party.
words.ex_cn: 他给了我关于惊喜派对的暗示。
words.en: A hint is a slight or indirect indication or suggestion.

words.ex: The police found a clue at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了一条线索。
words.en: A clue is an object or piece of information that helps to solve a problem or mystery.

words.tr: phrase. 一个微小的建议；轻微的暗示
words.ex: He gave me a slight suggestion about the project.
words.ex_cn: 他给了我一个关于这个项目的微小建议。

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.tr: phrase. 难以理解的；不容易明白的
words.ex: This math problem is hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学题很难理解。
words.en: Difficult to comprehend or interpret.

words.tr: adj. 挑剔的；吹毛求疵的
words.ex: He is picky about his food.
words.ex_cn: 他对食物很挑剔。
words.en: Someone who is picky is very careful about choosing only what they like.

words.tr: adj. 挑剔的；过分讲究的
words.ex: She is choosy about what she eats.
words.ex_cn: 她对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you describe someone as choosy, you mean they are very careful in choosing what they do or buy, and will only accept exactly what they want.

words.tr: adj. 爱挑剔的；过分讲究的
words.ex: He is fastidious about keeping his room clean.
words.ex_cn: 他非常讲究保持房间整洁。
words.en: Very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail.

words.ex: His viewpoint is different from mine.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与我的不同。
words.en: A viewpoint is a particular way of thinking about something, especially one that is influenced by your experiences or beliefs.

words.ex: From my point of view, this is the best choice.
words.ex_cn: 在我看来，这是最好的选择。
words.en: A particular attitude or way of considering a matter.

words.tr: n. 视角；观点；（对事物的）合理判断；
words.ex: His perspective on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的看法非常积极。
words.en: A particular attitude towards or way of regarding something; a point of view.

words.ex: From my standpoint, this plan is too risky.
words.ex_cn: 从我的立场来看，这个计划太冒险了。
words.en: A standpoint is a particular way of considering something, or a particular attitude towards it.

words.tr: adj. 特定的；明确的；具体的；
words.ex: He gave a specific reason for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个迟到的具体原因。
words.en: If someone is specific, they give a description that is precise and exact.

words.tr:
n. 混凝土；
adj. 具体的；
words.ex: The workers poured concrete to build the foundation.
words.ex_cn: 工人们浇筑混凝土来建造地基。
words.en: Concrete is a hard, strong construction material made by mixing a cementing material (such as Portland cement) and a mineral aggregate (such as sand and gravel) with sufficient water to cause the cement to set and bind the entire mass. In a broader sense, concrete can also refer to something that is tangible, specific, or real.

words.tr: adj. 可触摸的；实际的；有形的；确凿的；
words.ex: The statue is tangible and can be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像可以触摸，是实实在在的。
words.en: Something that is tangible is clear enough or definite enough to be easily seen, felt, or noticed.

words.tr:
n. 方面；尊重；尊敬；
v. 遵从；尊重；尊敬；
words.ex: In this respect, the plan is good.
words.ex_cn: 在这个方面，这个计划很好。
words.en: If you respect someone, you have a good opinion of their character or ideas.

words.ex: He earned the esteem of his colleagues through hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作赢得了同事们的尊重。
words.en: If you esteem someone or something, you respect or admire them.

words.ex: They think highly of their teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他们非常尊敬他们的老师。
words.en: To have a very good opinion of someone or something; to regard someone or something with great respect or admiration.

words.tr: adj. 刚愎自用的；顽固的；任性的
words.ex: He is headstrong and refuses to listen.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，不肯听别人的话。
words.en: If you refer to someone as headstrong, you are slightly critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to be advised by others.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；固执的；顽固的；
words.ex: He is obstinate and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很执拗，不肯改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obstinate, you are being critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to change their mind or be persuaded to do something else.

words.ex: He is stubborn and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很顽固，不肯改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is stubborn is determined to do what they want and is very unwilling to change their mind.

words.tr: adj. 黑暗的；幽暗的；忧郁的；沮丧的
words.ex: The room was gloomy with no windows.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间没有窗户，很黑暗。
words.en: If a place is gloomy, it is almost dark so that you cannot see very well. If people are gloomy, they are unhappy and have no hope.

words.tr:
adj. 黑暗的；暗色的；深色的；
n. 黑暗；夜；暗色；
words.ex: The room was dark after the power went out.
words.ex_cn: 停电后，房间变得黑暗。
words.en: The absence of light in a place is referred to as dark. It can also describe something that is not light in color, or something that is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.tr:
adj. 暗淡的；昏暗的；模糊的
v. （使）变暗淡；（使）变模糊；（使）减弱
words.ex: The room is dim because the lights are off.
words.ex_cn: 房间很暗，因为灯关了。
words.en: If a light or a place is dim, it is not bright or is not lit very strongly.

words.ex: The dog is huge.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗很大。
words.en: Extremely large in size or amount.

words.ex: The elephant is gigantic compared to a dog.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象相比狗来说是巨大的。
words.en: If you describe something as gigantic, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: The statue was colossal, taller than the building.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像巨大，比大楼还高。
words.en: If you describe something as colossal, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.tr: adj. 巨大的；大量的；辽阔的；
words.ex: The desert is vast and empty.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠巨大而空旷。
words.en: If you describe something as vast, you mean that it is very large.

words.ex: People use phones in modern times.
words.ex_cn: 在现代，人们使用手机。
words.en: The present era or period in history.

words.ex: We live in the contemporary age.
words.ex_cn: 我们生活在当代。

words.ex: He has prejudice against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人有偏见。
words.en: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

words.ex: The teacher showed a bias for students who arrived early.
words.ex_cn: 老师对早到的学生有偏爱。
words.en: If someone is biased, they prefer one group of people to another, and behave unfairly as a result.

words.ex: He showed partiality toward his favorite student.
words.ex_cn: 他对最喜欢的学生表现出偏袒。
words.en: If you have a partiality for something, you like it very much.

words.ex: He has a predilection for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: If you have a predilection for something, you have a strong liking for it.

words.ex: He has a preference for tea over coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他更喜欢茶而不是咖啡。
words.en: A preference is a greater liking for one alternative over another or others.

words.ex: The rain was unavoidable during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨期间，下雨是不可避免的。
words.en: If something is unavoidable, it cannot be avoided or prevented.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: The room was in chaos after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对之后，房间一片混乱。
words.en: A state of complete disorder and confusion.

words.ex: The children caused a big commotion in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在教室里制造了很大的喧闹。
words.en: A commotion is a lot of noise, confusion, and excitement.

words.ex: He looked at me with confusion.
words.ex_cn: 他困惑地看着我。
words.en: A state of uncertainty about what is happening, intended, or required.

words.ex: The noise from the construction caused a disturbance.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地的噪音造成了干扰。
words.en: A disturbance is an event or situation in which people behave in a noisy or violent way, or something that interrupts what you are doing.

words.tr: n. 骚动；骚乱；心烦意乱
words.ex: The crowd caused a tumult after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，人群引起了混乱。
words.en: A tumult is a state of confusion, noise, and excitement, often involving a large group of people.

words.ex: He gave an intentional wrong answer to confuse the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他故意答错答案来迷惑老师。
words.en: Something that is intentional is done on purpose, not by chance.

words.ex: He broke the vase on purpose.
words.ex_cn: 他故意打碎了花瓶。
words.en: If you do something on purpose, you do it intentionally, not by accident.

words.tr: adj. 打算中的；有意的； v. 打算；“intend”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The intended plan was to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 打算中的计划是去徒步旅行。
words.en: If something is intended for a particular purpose, it has been planned to fulfill that purpose.

words.tr: phrase. 详细的计划；精心制定的方案
words.ex: They have an elaborate plan for the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们有一个详尽的计划来完成这个项目。

words.tr: phrase. 经过长时间考虑之后
words.ex: After long deliberation, they decided to accept the offer.
words.ex_cn: 经过长时间深思熟虑后，他们决定接受这个提议。

words.ex: After careful thought, she decided to accept the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 经过深思熟虑，她决定接受这份工作。

words.ex: He will cancel the meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会取消会议。
words.en: If you cancel something that has been arranged, you stop it from happening. If you cancel an order for goods or services, you tell the person or organization supplying them that you no longer wish to receive them.

words.tr: v. 废除；取消；宣告无效
words.ex: The court will annul the marriage.
words.ex_cn: 法院将宣布婚姻无效。
words.en: To annul something means to declare it invalid or to officially say that it no longer exists.

words.ex: The government decided to abolish the old law.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定废除这项旧法律。
words.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

words.ex: He solved the crossword puzzle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快解开了这个填字谜。
words.en: If something puzzles you, you do not understand it and feel confused.

words.tr:
n. 谜语；费解的事
v. 解谜；出谜；使布满窟窿；打洞
words.ex: He told me a riddle and I solved it.
words.ex_cn: 他给我出了一道谜语，我解出来了。
words.en: A riddle is a question or statement that is deliberately very confusing and has a clever or amusing answer.

words.ex: The ancient symbol remains an enigma.
words.ex_cn: 这个古代符号仍然是一个谜。
words.en: An enigma is something that is mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.ex: You must abide by the school rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守校规。
words.en: To accept or act in accordance with a rule, decision, or recommendation.

words.ex: He must conform to the school rules.
words.ex_cn: 他必须遵守校规。
words.en: To comply with rules, standards, or laws; to behave according to socially acceptable conventions or standards.

words.ex: The scientist observe the birds every morning.
words.ex_cn: 科学家每天早上观察鸟类。
words.en: If you observe a person or thing, you watch them carefully, especially in order to learn something about them.

words.ex: You must comply with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: To act in accordance with a wish, command, or rule.

words.tr: adj. 热情的；充满热情的；
words.ex: She is passionate about teaching children.
words.ex_cn: 她对教孩子充满热情。
words.en: Having, showing, or caused by strong feelings or beliefs.

words.ex: He is an ardent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: An ardent person has strong feelings or enthusiasm for something.

words.ex: He is zealous about helping others.
words.ex_cn: 他热心帮助别人。
words.en: If someone is zealous, they are enthusiastic and eager about something, especially something they believe in very strongly.

words.ex: His answer was vague and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答不明确，难以理解。
words.en: If something written or spoken is vague, it does not explain or express things clearly.

words.ex: The storm destroyed the old bridge.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了那座旧桥。
words.en: To destroy something means to cause so much damage to it that it is completely ruined or does not exist any more.

words.tr:
n. 废墟；
v. 破坏；
words.ex: The old temple is now a ruin.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙现在已成为废墟。
words.en: Ruin means the physical destruction or disintegration of something or the state of disintegrating or being destroyed.

words.ex: The glass fell and broke to pieces on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃杯掉在地上，摔成了碎片。

words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: To devastate means to destroy or ruin something completely, or to cause someone to feel extreme sadness or shock.

words.tr: adj. 有技巧的；熟练的；灵巧的；
words.ex: He is a skillful painter who draws beautiful landscapes.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有技巧的画家，能画出美丽的风景。
words.en: Someone who is skillful at something does it very well.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.tr: adj. 灵巧的（手）；熟练的；敏捷的
words.ex: He is dexterous with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他双手很灵巧。
words.en: Someone who is dexterous is skillful with their hands.

words.tr:
adj. 警觉的；警惕的；
n. 警报；
v. （使）警惕；（使）戒备；
words.ex: The alert guard noticed the strange movement.
words.ex_cn: 这位警觉的警卫注意到了奇怪的动静。
words.en: If you are alert, you are paying full attention to things around you and are able to deal with anything that might happen.

words.ex: The watchful mother kept her eyes on the child.
words.ex_cn: 这位警惕的母亲一直盯着孩子。
words.en: If someone is watchful, they are careful to look for any danger or trouble.

words.tr: phrase. /adv. 警惕的；提防的；站岗的；戒备着的
words.ex: The soldier is on guard at the gate.
words.ex_cn: 士兵在门口站岗。
words.en: Being on guard means being watchful and alert to danger or trouble.

words.tr: phrase. 对……小心的；对……警惕的；对……谨慎提防的
words.ex: He is wary of strangers.
words.ex_cn: 他对陌生人保持警惕。
words.en: Cautious or wary about potential dangers or problems.

words.tr:
n. 熊；
v. 承受；忍受；带有；生（孩子）；
words.ex: A bear walked near the campsite.
words.ex_cn: 一只熊在露营地附近走动。
words.en: If you bear something, you accept it and are able to deal with it, even though it is unpleasant or painful. A bear is a large, strong wild animal with thick fur and sharp claws.

words.ex: I can't put up with his loud noise every night.
words.ex_cn: 我无法忍受他每晚的噪音。
words.en: To tolerate or endure something unpleasant or annoying.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.tr:
v. 站立；忍受；
n. 立足点；
words.ex: The boy stands near the door.
words.ex_cn: 男孩站在门附近。
words.en: If you stand somewhere, you are in an upright position with your feet on the ground. If something stands somewhere, it is in an upright position in that place.

words.ex: The old man walks slowly in the park.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人在公园里慢慢走路。
words.en: Having lived or existed for a long time; no longer young or new.

words.ex: The ancient Egyptians built the pyramids.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人建造了金字塔。
words.en: Belonging to the very distant past and no longer in existence.

words.ex: My ancestor came from China a hundred years ago.
words.ex_cn: 我的祖先一百年前来自中国。
words.en: An ancestor is a person from whom one is descended, typically more remote than a grandparent.

words.ex: The police found evidence at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了证据。
words.en: Evidence is anything that you see, experience, read, or are told that causes you to believe that something is true or has really happened.

words.ex: The facts show that he was not at the scene.
words.ex_cn: 事实表明他当时不在现场。
words.en: A fact is a piece of information that is known to be true.

words.ex: The math teacher asked for a proof of the theorem.
words.ex_cn: 数学老师要求给出这个定理的证明。
words.en: Proof is a fact, argument, or piece of evidence which shows that something is definitely true or definitely exists.

words.ex: The children are playing on the grounds.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在操场上玩耍。
words.en: Grounds can refer to the land surrounding a large building, such as a school or a hospital, or the reasons or justifications for a particular action or belief.

words.ex: His testimony proved the suspect was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 他的证词证明了嫌疑人是无辜的。
words.en: A formal written or spoken statement, especially one given in a court of law.

words.ex: He wears a helmet to protect his head.
words.ex_cn: 他戴头盔来保护头部。
words.en: If you protect someone or something, you prevent them from being harmed or damaged.

words.ex: The fence safeguards the garden from animals.
words.ex_cn: 围栏保护花园免受动物侵扰。
words.en: A safeguard is a measure taken to protect someone or something from potential harm or danger.

words.tr:
v. 保存；保护；保持；
n. （某群体）专有的活动；
words.ex: She preserves fresh fruit by making jam.
words.ex_cn: 她通过做果酱来保存新鲜水果。
words.en: To preserve something means to maintain it in its original or existing state.

words.tr:
n. 避难所；庇护所；
v. 庇护；遮蔽；
words.ex: The refugees found shelter in a small building.
words.ex_cn: 难民们在一个小建筑里找到了避难所。
words.en: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

words.ex: He inherited his family's heritage.
words.ex_cn: 他继承了家族的遗产。
words.en: Heritage refers to the traditions, achievements, beliefs, etc., that are part of the history of a group or nation.

words.ex: His legacy includes many charity schools.
words.ex_cn: 他的遗产包括许多慈善学校。
words.en: Something handed down from an ancestor or a predecessor or from the past.

words.ex: He received his father's watch as an inheritance.
words.ex_cn: 他收到了父亲留给他的手表作为遗产。
words.en: Inheritance is money or property which you receive from someone who has died.

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.tr: phrase. 公布；使知晓；公开；表明
words.ex: He wants to make known the truth about the event.
words.ex_cn: 他想让人们知道事件的真相。
words.en: To make information, facts, or feelings known means to tell people about them or to make them obvious.

words.ex: He refused to disclose the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝透露这个秘密。
words.en: To disclose information means to make it known to the public.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.ex: He violated the school rule by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: If someone violates an agreement, law, or promise, they break it.

words.tr: phrase. 侵犯；侵害；违背（权利、法律等）
words.ex: The new law cannot infringe on our rights.
words.ex_cn: 新法律不能侵犯我们的权利。
words.en: To encroach or trespass upon someone's rights, property, or privileges.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

words.ex: The microscope can magnify small objects.
words.ex_cn: 显微镜可以放大微小的物体。
words.en: To magnify something means to make it appear larger than it is, especially by using a lens or microscope. It can also mean to exaggerate or make something seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: The company plans to enlarge its office space.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划扩大其办公空间。
words.en: To make something bigger or more extensive.

words.ex: They will extend the deadline by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他们将截止日期延长一周。
words.en: To extend something means to make it longer or larger, or to spread it over a larger area.

words.ex: He tries to aggrandize himself by lying about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他通过吹嘘自己的成就来抬高自己。
words.en: To increase the power, status, or wealth of someone or something.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: The loud noise frightened the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音吓到了孩子。
words.en: If something or someone frightens you, they cause you to suddenly feel afraid, anxious, or nervous.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: Passion is the driving force behind her success.
words.ex_cn: 热情是她成功的驱动力。
words.en: A driving force is a person or thing that has a very powerful effect on what happens or on how people behave.

words.ex: The team gained momentum after scoring the first goal.
words.ex_cn: 球队在进第一个球后获得了势头。
words.en: Momentum is the ability of something to keep increasing, developing, or being more successful.

words.ex: This is a genuine diamond.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石。
words.en: If something is genuine, it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.tr: adj. 真实的；真的；真正的；
words.ex: This is a real diamond, not fake.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石，不是假的。
words.en: Something that is real actually exists and is not imagined, invented, or theoretical.

words.ex: He is an eccentric man who wears socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他是个古怪的人，穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: If you say that someone is eccentric, you mean that they behave in a strange way, and have habits or opinions that are different from those of most people.

words.ex: This town has a peculiar custom of dancing at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有一个独特的午夜跳舞习俗。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as peculiar, you think that they are strange or unusual, sometimes in an unpleasant way.

words.tr: adj. 奇怪的；奇数的；余的；
words.ex: He wore an odd hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇怪的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odd, you mean that they are strange or unusual.

words.ex: The two colors are distinct.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色有区别。
words.en: If something is distinct, it is easily seen, heard, or understood.

words.tr:
adj. 清楚的；明确的；清晰的；清澈的；晴朗的；
v. 清空；清除；放晴；使明确；
adv. 清楚地；彻底地；
words.ex: The instructions are clear.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很清楚。
words.en: Free from anything that marks or darkens; transparent; bright; not obscure or ambiguous; easily understood; free from guilt or blame.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.ex: It is obvious that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is obvious, it is easy to see or understand.

words.tr:
v. 伪造；假装；冒充；
adj. 假的；冒充的；伪造的；
words.ex: He faked a signature to get the money.
words.ex_cn: 他伪造了一个签名来拿到钱。
words.en: If something is fake, it is not real, genuine, or true, but is made to appear so.

words.ex: The news was false.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻是虚假的。
words.en: If something is false, it is incorrect, untrue, or mistaken.

words.ex: He tried to counterfeit money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图伪造货币。
words.en: Made in exact imitation of something valuable with the intention to deceive or defraud.

words.tr: adj. 盛行的；有优势的；普遍的； v. “prevail”的现在分词；
words.ex: The prevailing weather today is sunny.
words.ex_cn: 今天盛行的天气是晴天。
words.en: The prevailing thing in a particular place or at a particular time is the one that is most common or strongest at that place or time.

words.tr: adj. 常见的；普通的；共有的；
words.ex: Colds are a common illness in winter.
words.ex_cn: 感冒在冬天是很常见的疾病。
words.en: Something that is common happens often or is found in many places.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的；
words.ex: Smoking is prevalent in that country.
words.ex_cn: 在那个国家，吸烟很普遍。
words.en: If a condition, practice, or belief is prevalent, it is common or widespread.

words.tr:
n. 跨栏；障碍；难关
v. 越过障碍；克服
words.ex: He jumped over the hurdle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速跳过了跨栏。
words.en: A hurdle is a problem or difficulty that you must deal with before you can achieve something.

words.ex: The big rock was an obstacle on the road.
words.ex_cn: 那块大石头是路上的障碍。
words.en: An obstacle is something which makes it difficult for you to go forward or to achieve something.

words.ex: He faced difficulty in solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决这道数学题时遇到了困难。
words.en: A difficulty is a problem or issue that is hard to deal with or understand.

words.tr:
n. 挑战；
v. 提出挑战；
words.ex: Climbing that mountain is a big challenge.
words.ex_cn: 爬那座山是一个巨大的挑战。
words.en: A challenge is something new and difficult which requires great effort and determination.

words.tr: adj. 艰苦的；强硬的；严厉的；
words.ex: The hike was tough but beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 这次徒步旅行很艰苦但很美丽。
words.en: A tough person is strong and determined, and can tolerate difficulty or suffering.

words.tr: n. 标准；尺度；准则；“criterion”的复数；
words.ex: The main criteria for selection are skill and experience.
words.ex_cn: 选择的主要标准是技能和经验。
words.en: A criterion is a standard or principle by which something is judged or decided.

words.tr:
n. 标准；
adj. 标准的；规范的；
words.ex: The school has a high standard for homework.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校对作业有很高的标准。
words.en: A standard is a level of quality or achievement, especially a level that is thought to be acceptable.

words.tr:
n. 限制；
v. 限制；
words.ex: The teacher set a limit on homework time.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作业时间设定了限制。
words.en: A limit is the greatest amount, extent, or degree of something that is possible.

words.ex: The law restricts driving after drinking.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制酒后驾驶。
words.en: to limit the movements or actions of someone, or to limit something and reduce its size or prevent it from increasing

words.tr:
n. 经常重复的评价（或抱怨）；叠句；
v. 克制；
words.ex: His constant refrain is that the food is too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他经常抱怨食物太贵。
words.en: If you refrain from doing something, you deliberately do not do it.

words.ex: He tries to restrain his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他努力克制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you restrain someone, you stop them from doing what they intended or wanted to do, usually by using your physical strength.

words.tr: phrase. 限制在范围内；控制在限度内
words.ex: I must keep my spending within limits.
words.ex_cn: 我必须把我的花费限制在范围内。

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.tr: phrase. 控制；抑制；使受约束
words.ex: Parents must keep in check their children's screen time.
words.ex_cn: 父母必须控制孩子的屏幕时间。
words.en: To restrain or control something to prevent it from becoming excessive or unmanageable.

words.ex: He wears conventional clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿传统服装去上班。
words.en: Conventional ideas, methods, or systems are the ones that are generally accepted and used, and that have been used for a long time.

words.ex: He wears traditional clothes on holidays.
words.ex_cn: 他在节日时穿传统服装。
words.en: Traditional refers to customs, beliefs, or methods that have existed for a long time without changing.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.ex: He finally admit his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, you agree, often unwillingly, that it is true.

words.ex: He finally acknowledged his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: He confesses that he made a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他承认自己犯了一个错误。
words.en: If you confess to doing something, you admit that you did it.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.tr: phrase. 意见冲突；观点碰撞
words.ex: There was a clash of opinion between the two friends.
words.ex_cn: 两个朋友之间发生了意见冲突。

words.ex: He denies taking the money.
words.ex_cn: 他否认拿了钱。
words.en: To deny means to declare that something is not true, or to refuse to give or grant something.

words.ex: The company will withhold his salary until he signs the contract.
words.ex_cn: 公司会扣留他的工资，直到他签署合同。
words.en: If you withhold something that someone wants, you refuse to let them have it.

words.ex: He tries to negate the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图否认事实。
words.en: If someone negates something, they say that it does not exist or is not true.

words.ex: The school changed its curriculum last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年学校更改了课程。
words.en: A curriculum is the subjects that are studied in a school, college, or university.

words.ex: The course of the river changed after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 河流的流程在洪水后发生了变化。
words.en: A course is a series of lessons or lectures on a particular subject.

words.ex: The teacher gave us the syllabus for the course.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了我们这门课的教学大纲。
words.en: A syllabus is an outline or summary of the main points of a text, lecture, or course of study.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；杰出的；罕见的；特别的；
words.ex: She is an exceptional student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 她是一名卓越的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: An exceptional person or thing has some unusual quality or ability that makes them different from others.

words.ex: She is a good student.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个好学生。
words.en: Something that is good is of a high quality, standard, or level.

words.tr: adj. 优秀的；杰出的；卓越的；
words.ex: He got an excellent score on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试中取得了优异的成绩。
words.en: Something that is excellent is very good indeed.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；极好的；明亮的；灿烂的；
words.ex: He gave a brilliant answer to the math question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这道数学题给出了卓越的回答。
words.en: A brilliant person, idea, or performance is extremely clever or skilful.

words.ex: His speech was very impressive.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲非常令人印象深刻。
words.en: Something that is impressive makes you admire it because it is very good, large, important, etc.

words.ex: Her courage in facing danger is admirable.
words.ex_cn: 她在面对危险时表现出的勇气令人钦佩。
words.en: If you say that something is admirable, you mean that you approve of it or respect it.

words.ex: The dog follows its owner every day.
words.ex_cn: 狗每天跟随它的主人。
words.en: To go or come after (a person or thing proceeding ahead); move or travel behind.

words.tr:
n. 踪迹；轨道；小路；跑道；
v. 追踪；跟踪；
words.ex: The dog followed the track of the rabbit.
words.ex_cn: 狗跟着兔子的踪迹。
words.en: A track is a path or route along which something moves or travels. It can also refer to marks left by something that has passed, or the act of following such marks to find someone or something.

words.ex: The dog wagged its tail happily.
words.ex_cn: 狗开心地摇着尾巴。
words.en: The tail of an animal, bird, or fish is the part extending beyond the end of its body.

words.ex: The tree casts a long shadow at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 夕阳下，树投下长长的影子。
words.en: A shadow is a dark shape on a surface that is made when something stands between a light and the surface.

words.tr:
n. 猎犬
v. 追逐；纠缠
words.ex: The hound chased the rabbit through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 猎犬在森林里追赶兔子。
words.en: A hound is a type of dog used for hunting or chasing. It can also refer to someone who persistently pursues or bothers someone else.

words.tr:
n. 茎；柄；梗
v. 跟踪；偷偷接近；昂首阔步地走
words.ex: The stalk of the sunflower is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 向日葵的茎很高。
words.en: The main stem of a plant, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean. Also, to pursue or approach stealthily.

words.ex: The GPS can pinpoint your exact location.
words.ex_cn: GPS可以精准定位你的准确位置。
words.en: To pinpoint something means to locate or identify it precisely.

words.ex: The doctor can diagnose the illness quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生能很快诊断出这种病。
words.en: If someone or something is diagnosed as having a particular illness or problem, their illness or problem is identified. If an illness or problem is diagnosed, it is identified.

words.ex: He was reluctant to leave his home.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意离开家。
words.en: If you are reluctant to do something, you are unwilling to do it and hesitate before doing it, or do it slowly and without enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 不愿意的；不情愿的；
words.ex: He was unwilling to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意帮助他的朋友。
words.en: If you are unwilling to do something, you do not want to do it and will not agree to do it.

words.tr: phrase. 拖延；磨蹭；故意放慢行动
words.ex: If you keep dragging your feet, we will miss the bus.
words.ex_cn: 如果你继续拖拖拉拉，我们就会错过公交车。
words.en: To delay or procrastinate intentionally.

words.tr: adj. 不情愿做某事；勉强做某事

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.ex: He stayed home because of illness.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病待在家里。
words.en: An illness is a particular disease, especially one that is not very serious.

words.ex: The doctor treated his disease with medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生用药物治疗了他的疾病。
words.en: A disease is an illness that affects people, animals, or plants, often caused by infection or a failure of health rather than by an accident.

words.ex: The virus made many people sick.
words.ex_cn: 这个病毒让很多人病了。
words.en: A virus is a very small organism that causes infectious diseases in people, animals, and plants.

words.ex: A bug crawled on the leaf.
words.ex_cn: 一只小虫子爬在叶子上。
words.en: A bug is a small insect, or it can refer to a fault in a computer program or system.

words.ex: The wound caused a serious infection.
words.ex_cn: 伤口引起了严重的感染。
words.en: An infection is a disease caused by microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, or parasites invading the body.

words.ex: She combines flour and water to make dough.
words.ex_cn: 她把面粉和水混合在一起做面团。
words.en: To combine means to join or merge two or more things together to form a single entity.

words.tr:
n. 混合；结合；
v. 混合；掺入；合成；交往；
words.ex: The recipe calls for a mix of flour and sugar.
words.ex_cn: 这个食谱需要一种面粉和糖的混合物。
words.en: To combine two or more substances so that they become a single substance, or to be combined in this way.

words.ex: Please stir the soup before serving.
words.ex_cn: 请在上菜前搅拌一下汤。
words.en: To mix a substance or move it around using a spoon or other object; to cause to move or act; to arouse or excite.

words.ex: She blends flour and water to make dough.
words.ex_cn: 她把面粉和水混合在一起做面团。
words.en: To mix substances together so that they combine into a single substance.

words.ex: The barn is used for storage of grain.
words.ex_cn: 这个谷仓用于粮食的贮存。
words.en: The act of storing something or the space where things are stored.

words.ex: She keeps the room clean every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天保持房间干净。
words.en: To continue to have or hold something; to maintain a condition or position.

words.ex: The weather is unpredictable today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气不可预测。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unpredictable, you mean that you cannot tell what they are going to do or how they are going to behave.

words.tr: adj. 不可预见的；无法预料的
words.ex: The storm was unforeseeable.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴是无法预见的。
words.en: If something is unforeseeable, it cannot be predicted or known about before it happens.

words.tr: v. 波动，涨落，起伏( fluctuate的过去式和过去分词 )
words.ex: The price fluctuated last week.
words.ex_cn: 上周价格波动了。
words.en: If something fluctuates, it changes a lot in an irregular way.
